## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

 Computational analysis via DharmaNexus confirms this close relationship, recording substantial overlap between Tha-Ap 512 (§0.1–11.1) and Tha-Ap 469 (§0.1–10.1), alongside 114 matching segments across 43 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest Pali reuse partner is the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (Paṭhamo bhāgo), which shares extended passages with the text (§0.3–7.1) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, recurring stock verses—particularly those describing the offering of fruit and its resulting karmic trajectory—are shared extensively with other apadānas of fruit donors, including *Labujadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 384), *Piyālaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 502), and *Kapitthaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 514) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matches, DharmaNexus detects low-level formulaic alignments with the Tibetan translation of the *Suvarṇavarṇāvadāna* (D4144) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
